Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the sync this week. Attached is a lean mutual action map (MAP) + evaluation checklist we discussed for the PoC focused on streaming chat TTFT and concurrency behavior. High-level asks from our side:

- Agreed PoC scope: 2-week evaluation on redwood-dedicated with sample endpoints (chat stream).
- Acceptance criteria (initial): TTFT p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 700ms under targeted concurrency profile (1, 5, 20). Streaming tail latency p95 target <= 300ms.
- Test data: 1k synthetic sessions (30k tokens avg / session) + 50 canonical user prompts you provided.
- Security: we’ll pull logs to a customer-only S3 bucket (read-only for Lighthouse) and redact any PHI before transfer.
- Timeline: start perf runs Mon Oct 5, core results by Thu Oct 8, mutual sign-off by Fri Oct 9.

I’ve attached: MVP-Eval-Checklist (spreadsheet), a runbook for the streaming harness, and the empty MAP we can iterate on. Can you confirm the test windows and whether you need us to run in eu/us regions or a specific VPC?

Thanks — I’ve looped in Laura (PM) and Ben (SE) to own the bench and schedule.

— Mateo

Alex — thanks for the quick turn. We agree: treat p99 degradation at highest concurrency as "conditional pass" if there is a documented mitigation and a timeline for improvement. I updated the MAP to include a mitigation bucket for batching/kv cache sizing and a rollback path to a smaller model if necessary.

Bench details we’ll run (summary):
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated (4x A100 80GB equivalent nodes), us-west-2, model: open-llm-chat-v3-quant (redwood-verified variant).
- Harness: continuous streaming client with realistic typing delays, token-accurate counters; 3 concurrency profiles: 1, 5, 20 users.
- Metrics collected: TTFT (time to first token), streaming latency per-token (ms), tokens/sec throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, kv cache hit ratio, p50/p95/p99 for both TTFT and streaming tail.
- Acceptance thresholds (finalized): TTFT p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 700ms (target); streaming tail p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 600ms.

Ben — can you schedule the bench for Mon Oct 5 in the us-west-2 slot and push artifacts to the shared drive. We’ll produce a short CSV and a one-sheet summary for the MAP.

Mateo

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action map & Lighthouse streaming TTFT evaluation — first run results

Team — ran the initial suite in us-west-2 this morning. Summary CSV attached; highlights below. Full artifact is on the shared drive.

Test matrix: 1, 5, 20 concurrent simulated user sessions; each session ~30k tokens total, average prompt length ~35 tokens, streaming enabled.

Key results (median of 3 runs each):
- Concurrency 1:
  - TTFT p50: 120ms; p95: 180ms; p99: 320ms
  - Streaming tail p50: 40ms; p95: 120ms; p99: 260ms
  - Tokens/sec (aggregate): 2400
- Concurrency 5:
  - TTFT p50: 140ms; p95: 260ms; p99: 520ms
  - Streaming tail p50: 50ms; p95: 170ms; p99: 420ms
  - Tokens/sec (aggregate): 10,300
- Concurrency 20:
  - TTFT p50: 190ms; p95: 420ms; p99: 980ms
  - Streaming tail p50: 70ms; p95: 320ms; p99: 1,600ms
  - Tokens/sec (aggregate): 36,800

Observations:
- Pass/Fail: Concurrency 1 and 5 meet acceptance thresholds. Concurrency 20 breaches TTFT p99 and streaming tail p95/p99 significantly.
- Resource signals: GPU utilization peaked ~88% at concurrency 20; kernel queueing observed consistent with kv cache thrashing at long session lengths.
- Deterministic pins: The model quantization variant shows slightly higher p99 under long-token sessions — we recommend re-running with a different kernel selection (less aggressive int8 path) as a mitigation.

Attached: lh-map-performance-results.csv, streaming-ttft-screenshots.png (latency histograms), bench-config.yaml

Next steps proposed:
1) Run an experiment switching kernel selection + increased kv-cache size (ETA: 24–36hrs).
2) If p99 still > 900ms at concurrency 20, propose a staged rollout plan in the MAP: limit concurrency per endpoint + queueing fallback.
3) Drafted a short summary slide for your leadership — will share by Tue Oct 6.
